WHAT YOU NEED TO DO
Evaluate Entrepreneurial Ideas
Evaluating the idea:
Do I believe the idea genuinely feasible?
Is this a new idea (given my target market)?
Can I make a profit by implementing the idea - even in the long term?
Ask others what they think about your idea and how they would rate it?
Try it out for real and obtain live feedback!
o Try things out because you won’t know in advance if an idea will work
o Don’t use too many resources in the experiment - remember it might not work
o You’ll have a better understanding if something works after you have tried it. Don’t
rely on your instinct alone
o Sometimes things that go wrong lead to new ideas e.g. marketing a product or
adding an extra service. Things that don’t work out are often experiments in disguise
EVALUATING A NEW IDEA :
EXPERIMENTING WITHOUT INVESTING TOO MANY

EXERCISE :
Experiment to identify the weak spots as well as the
potential!
Denise overhears friends complaining about the price of cosmetics.
She’s also aware many imported products contain lots of chemical
additives. Denise thinks that starting a range of organic cosmetics
adapted for the skin of Kenyan women could be a good idea. Now she
wants to find out if her idea has potential.
INSTRUCTION: Work in pairs (02).
How can Denise test her idea?
Create an experiment to see if the idea is promising or not. Answer the following
questions:
o What problems might happen during the experiment?
o What might Esther learn from these problems?
